title: What type is it?
brief:
The list values holds four different kinds of value. Print the type of each one, one per line, in the same order as the list.

Python has a function called type() that tells you the type of a value. print(type(42)) shows <class 'int'>.

vocabulary.gloss: a function that tells you what kind of value something is
a collection of values in order, written in square brackets
a number with a decimal point, like 3.5
a value that is True or False

starterCode:
values = [42, "hello", 3.5, True]

# Print the type of each value in the list, one per line

tests.name: prints all four types in order

hints: You can get one value from a list with its position in square brackets. The first value is values[0], the second is values[1].
Print the type of the first value like this: print(type(values[0])). Then do the same for positions 1, 2 and 3.
Four print lines is fine. If you know for loops already, for value in values: print(type(value)) does the same job in two lines.
solution:
values = [42, "hello", 3.5, True]

print(type(values[0]))
print(type(values[1]))
print(type(values[2]))
print(type(values[3]))
